paper_title: DeltaEdit Enhancing Sequential Editing in Large Language Models by   Controlling Superimposed Noise
caption: : labelformat=parens, labelsep=period

model_annotations.English: This plot, titled "GPT2-XL," illustrates the performance metrics Efficacy$_{top}$ and $noise_E$ for AlphaEdit and DeltaEdit. The x-axis, which lacks a text label, employs a linear scale with plotted data points ranging from approximately 200 to 3000, featuring numeric tick marks spaced at regular intervals of 500. The plot utilizes dual y-axes to accommodate different metrics. The primary y-axis on the left is labeled "Efficacy$_{top}$" and follows a linear scale ranging from 86 to 100 with a tick interval of 2. The secondary y-axis on the right is labeled "$noise_E$" and follows a linear scale ranging from 2 to 12, also with a tick interval of 2. Four distinct lines represent the data. The AlphaEdit Efficacy$_{top}$ line is shown as a light red dashed line with square markers corresponding to the left y-axis; it begins at approximately 99.5 at x=200, exhibits a gradual decline to roughly 95.8 at x=2000, and drops to an ending value of about 86.0 at x=3000. The DeltaEdit Efficacy$_{top}$ line, also mapped to the left y-axis, is a light purple dashed line with square markers; it starts near 99.5 at x=200, decreases to 97.1 at x=2000, and finishes at roughly 93.8 at x=3000. The AlphaEdit $noise_E$ line corresponds to the right y-axis and is displayed as a light red solid line with circular markers; it demonstrates a steady upward trend from a starting value of approximately 2.8 at x=200 to a final value of about 12.0 at x=3000. Lastly, the DeltaEdit $noise_E$ line, mapped to the right y-axis, is depicted as a light purple solid line with circular markers; it shows a continuous increase from roughly 2.3 at x=200 to an ending value of approximately 11.4 at x=3000.
model_annotations.German: The line plot, titled "GPT2-XL," illustrates the performance of two editing methods, AlphaEdit and DeltaEdit, measured by two different metrics across a sequence of data points. The plot features an unlabelled linear x-axis with values ranging from approximately 200 to 3000, displaying major tick marks that begin at 500 and are spaced at intervals of 500. There are two linear y-axes: the left y-axis is labeled "Efficacy_{top}" with values ranging from 86 to 100 in increments of 2, while the right y-axis is labeled "noise_E" with values ranging from 2 to 12 in increments of 2. The dashed light red line with square markers represents AlphaEdit Efficacy_{top} mapped to the left y-axis; it begins at approximately 99.5, experiences a gradual decline to roughly 98.8 at x=1000, and then declines more steeply to finish at exactly 86 at x=3000. The dashed light purple line with square markers denotes DeltaEdit Efficacy_{top}, also mapped to the left y-axis, starting near 99.5 at the beginning of the x-axis and demonstrating a steady decline to end at approximately 93.8 at x=3000. The solid light red line with circular markers indicates AlphaEdit noise_E, corresponding to the right y-axis; it starts at approximately 2.8 and exhibits a continuous, upward trend across the entire x-axis, culminating at exactly 12 at x=3000. Finally, the solid light purple line with circular markers represents DeltaEdit noise_E, which maps to the right y-axis, begins at approximately 2.3, rises steadily across the plot, and reaches an ending value of approximately 11.4 at x=3000.
